Tuition statistics are a starting point, not the full student budget

Two official tuition graphics and two budget scenarios separate preliminary 2026/2027 averages from the costs and funding of an individual study plan.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 4 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Two fixed official-data graphics are separate from the editable budget. The tuition input begins at the published Canadian undergraduate national average, but a personal budget needs the actual institution/program quote. All other defaults are hypothetical. Tuition is entered once and is not prorated when living-cost months change. No grants, tax credits, loan approval, fee forecast or investment return is calculated; confirmed funding is entered separately. Source weighted tuition is not a full cost-of-attendance estimate or a promise about any student’s bill.

The central idea

Use an average to frame the question, then replace it with the actual tuition quote and add the other costs. A tuition figure alone cannot establish how much cash a student needs.

01

Read the official numbers with their population and period

Statistics Canada’s Table 37-10-0045-01 reports preliminary 2026/2027 national undergraduate tuition averages of CAD 8,021 for Canadian students and CAD 42,062 for international students. The first graphic presents those published observations, rather than values calculated from the budget controls.

These are weighted averages for full-time students at public degree-granting institutions, expressed in current dollars. They are tuition amounts, not complete living budgets or individual program quotations. The difference between the groups can reflect different program and institution mixes.

The ten-province graphic shows the Canadian undergraduate observations from the same release. It includes no territory. A province’s bar is not the price every student pays there, and a lower average does not rank the quality or overall affordability of a particular program.

02

Keep a weighted average separate from a personal quote

The survey methodology explains how institutions report fees and how enrolment weights are used to combine them. The current table uses 2023/2024 enrolment weights. The national estimate is not a simple average of the provincial bars.

A weighted mean is also different from a median. These bars do not say that half of students pay less than the displayed amount, and they provide no price range for a particular program.

Program mix and residency treatment also affect comparisons. Some provincial averages incorporate different fees for in-province and out-of-province Canadian students. The source marks the current academic year preliminary, even though the selected CSV status cells are blank.

The data were released on 16 September 2026 and retrieved for this article on 25 October 2026. The two observation charts remain fixed when the controls change. For a personal plan, replace the editable tuition value with the institution’s quote and confirm which fees that quote includes.

03

Add the costs that tuition does not cover

The default budget starts at the published CAD 8,021 Canadian undergraduate national average. The remaining amounts are hypothetical: CAD 1,000 of additional compulsory fees, CAD 1,000 of books and equipment, and CAD 1,000 of travel and setup.

Living and local transport are budgeted at CAD 1,400 a month for eight months, adding CAD 11,200. The resulting modeled total is CAD 22,221. Tuition is about 36.10% of this particular example; that share is not a population estimate of what students generally spend.

The waterfall expresses all the cost lines and confirmed funding in CAD. Check for overlap when entering real amounts: a residence package might already include food, or a quoted fee might already include a compulsory charge. Each actual cost belongs in the ledger once.

04

Subtract confirmed resources without treating borrowing as a price reduction

The example enters CAD 12,000 of confirmed funding, leaving CAD 10,221 to arrange under the selected budget. The funding input does not calculate grants, scholarships, tax benefits, family support or loan approval.

A loan can supply cash for a bill while creating a separate repayment obligation. If borrowing is included in confirmed funding, the budget gap may close without the underlying education cost becoming smaller. Record that repayment plan separately.

A negative waterfall endpoint means entered funding exceeds this budget; the additional-funding metric is then floored at zero. The tool assigns no destination to the surplus. A zero-cost example reports that no modeled cost share is available rather than dividing by zero.

05

Test the living-cost calendar and revise the plan

The matrix varies monthly living costs and the number of months to cover. Tuition, fees, books, setup and confirmed funding remain selected. A twelve-month living plan therefore adds summer costs without automatically changing the tuition entry.

The model does not prorate tuition when the living-cost duration changes. Tuition schedules can depend on programs, credits, terms and status, so the quote needs its own review. The matrix contains hypothetical allowances and is not an accommodation-price survey.

Use the observed averages as context, then build a dated personal cost and funding list. The charts distinguish an official statistical benchmark from the cash a particular plan needs, while leaving enrolment choices, funding approval and account-withdrawal rules to their own evidence.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. Charts labelled “Official statistics” or “Derived from official statistics” identify their source periods. Other charts are hypothetical scenarios. Original scenario calculations and research checklists are TickerLantern’s educational analysis; attributed publisher examples retain their stated source and scope. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.

  2. Statistics Canada · Tuition and Living Accommodation Costs methodology ↗

    Survey scope, weighting and preliminary-year treatment. The source metadata identifies 2023/2024 enrolment weights for the current release; program and residency composition affect comparison.
